## Appendix — pinned texts

### dispatch-serial.md (canonical `scaffold/hosts/claude/.claude/skills/sprint-execution/dispatch-serial.md`)

```markdown
# Serial Dispatch Contract

This contract is the dispatch path for a host whose adapter declares `dispatchMode: serial` — a host with no Workflow primitive. It replaces the playbook's wave launch (§C.0.1) and nothing else: §22 (autonomy and the five true-blocker kinds), the per-story steps §C.1–§C.9, every role boundary, and every rule in `cleargate-enforcement.md` apply unchanged. A host that declares `dispatchMode: wave-parallel` never uses this file.

## 1. When this contract applies

- The installed playbook for this host names this file in §2 and §C.0.
- `dispatchMode` is fixed when ClearGate is installed. It is never chosen per session, and it is never a fallback for a host that has a Workflow primitive but cannot reach it — that host halts (§C.0).

## 2. The serial loop

Run the waves in `.cleargate/sprint-runs/<sprint-id>/plans/waves.json` order and, inside a wave, its stories in `stories` order. Exactly one story is in flight at any time, and inside a story exactly one role dispatch is in flight at any time.

1. Ask for the next action:
   `node .cleargate/scripts/dispatch_serial.mjs next --sprint <sprint-id> --wave <wave-id>`
   It prints one JSON object. Act on its `action`:
   - `process-flashcards` (exit 4) — process every listed card exactly as §C.9 says (approve or reject, then write its `.processed-<hash>` marker), then ask again.
   - `dispatch` (exit 0) — continue with step 2 for the named `storyId`.
   - `halt` (exit 3) — a recorded verdict for this story is not GREEN. Stop and surface its blocker to the human in this turn.
   - `wave-complete` (exit 0) — go to the next wave.
2. Create the story's worktree with exactly the printed `worktreeCommand` — `git worktree add .worktrees/STORY-X -b story/STORY-X sprint/S-NN` — unless `worktreeExists` is `true`.
3. Run the story through §C.1–§C.7. Each role works only inside `.worktrees/STORY-X`, plus its report under `.cleargate/sprint-runs/<sprint-id>/reports/`. Dispatch one role, wait for its final report, then decide the next dispatch. Never start a second role while one is still running.
4. Write the story's verdict (§5) to a file and record it:
   `node .cleargate/scripts/dispatch_serial.mjs record --sprint <sprint-id> --wave <wave-id> --verdict <file>`
   Exit 0: the verdict is GREEN — go back to step 1. Exit 3: the verdict is not GREEN — halt now, in this turn, and dispatch nothing else. Exit 1: the verdict is malformed — fix the verdict, never the validator.

## 3. Invariants reproduced

| Invariant | How the serial path keeps it |
|---|---|
| One ClearGate-managed worktree per story, cut from the sprint branch | `next` prints the command the wave path builds (`worktreeAddCommand` in `launch_wave.mjs`); worktrees are created one at a time |
| Flashcard write-gate per story (`cleargate-enforcement.md` §4.3) | `next` refuses to name the next story until every flagged card has a `.processed-<hash>` marker; the host's dispatch hook enforces the same gate (§4.6) at every role dispatch |
| Exactly-once dispatch attribution | the host's own dispatch hook chain attributes each role dispatch once (a dispatch marker or sentinel, claimed when the subagent stops); never write attribution by hand |
| Single-writer serial merge | DevOps merges each GREEN story to `sprint/S-NN` (§C.7) before the next story starts |
| True-blocker halt (§22) | a non-GREEN verdict halts the loop synchronously in the orchestrator's own turn |
| Idempotent resume | `next --resume` re-dispatches only the blocked story, reuses its worktree, and never re-dispatches a GREEN story |

## 4. Deliberately omitted

These three mechanisms exist only to work around a parallel wave; copying them would weaken the serial path.

| Mechanism (wave path) | Why the wave path has it | Why this contract omits it |
|---|---|---|
| `SKIP_FLASHCARD_GATE=1` for the whole wave | a parallel dispatch cannot give each segment its own environment, so the write-gate is relocated to the barrier | one story runs at a time, so the original per-story gate (§4.3) applies unmodified; setting the variable would silently widen the flashcard blind spot. Never set it during a serial run. |
| `RUN_ID`-keyed barrier ledger rows | under a Workflow run the dispatch hook never fires and the subagent stop event carries the orchestrator's session | serial dispatches go through the host's own dispatch hook chain; where the host exposes no verifiable usage, no usage row is written at all |
| Verdict returned instead of halting | a parallel run cannot stop for a human mid-run | the serial loop halts in its own turn, which is strictly stronger |

## 5. Verdict

Every story ends with one verdict object — the protocol §23.1 envelope, validated with `validateVerdicts(verdicts, { mode: 'serial' })`:

- `verdict` (`GREEN`, `ESCALATED` or `BLOCKED`), `storyId`, `runId` (the `runId` that `next` printed), `counters` (`qa_bounces`, `arch_bounces`, `breaker_hits`) and `flashcards_flagged` (the union of the dev and QA reports' cards).
- `devSha`, `qaSha`: required on GREEN; `null` on a non-GREEN verdict when that commit does not exist. Never invent a SHA.
- `tokens`: the measured object when the host reports verifiable usage, otherwise exactly `{ "metering": "unavailable" }`. Never zeros.
- `blocker` (`type`, `message`): required on a non-GREEN verdict; `type` is one of the five §22 kinds.

## 6. Resume after a blocker

After the human resolves a blocker, run `node .cleargate/scripts/dispatch_serial.mjs next --sprint <sprint-id> --wave <wave-id> --resume`. It names the blocked story again (`worktreeExists: true`). Run it from the step the blocker interrupted, record its new verdict, and continue with step 1. GREEN stories are never re-dispatched.
```

There is one and only one way a sprint executes on this host, and it has no toggle. Every rule in `cleargate-enforcement.md` is **always enforced** (`CLEARGATE_ADVISORY=1` is the sole break-glass, and it only softens gate *strength*, never the execution path). There is no parallel wave launch on this host and no other loop.

**R2** (A2):
```
### C.0 Execution — the serial dispatch contract (`dispatch-serial.md`)

Run every wave from the Architect's `waves.json` through `dispatch-serial.md`: one story in flight at a time, in wave order, each in its own ClearGate-managed `.worktrees/STORY-X` cut from `sprint/S-NN`; the flashcard gate between every pair of consecutive stories; and a synchronous halt, in your own turn, on any non-GREEN verdict. `node .cleargate/scripts/dispatch_serial.mjs next` names the next action and `… record` validates and records each story's verdict. The per-story steps §C.1–§C.9 below are the body of each serial step.
```

**R3** (A3):
```
**Serial merge.** Stories run one at a time, so DevOps merges each GREEN `story/STORY-X` to `sprint/S-NN` as soon as that story passes — one worktree at a time, never two concurrently; `sprint/S-NN` is a single-writer axis. A story whose verdict is not GREEN is not merged: record its verdict and halt (`dispatch-serial.md` §2). After the human resolves the blocker, `dispatch_serial.mjs next --resume` re-dispatches only that story.
```

**R4** (A4):
```
The dispatch hook (`pending-task-sentinel.sh`, registered for `Agent|.*spawn_agent`) blocks the next role dispatch until every card has a `.processed-<hash>` marker, and `dispatch_serial.mjs next` will not name the next story until they exist.

**Per-story gate.** On this host the gate runs between every pair of consecutive stories. It is never relocated and never suppressed: do not set `SKIP_FLASHCARD_GATE` during a sprint (`dispatch-serial.md` §4).
```

### protocol §23.5 (canonical `scaffold/core/.cleargate/knowledge/cleargate-protocol.md`, after §23.4)

```
### 23.5 Serial dispatch contract (`dispatchMode: serial`)

Hosts without a Workflow primitive run every wave one story at a time through `.cleargate/scripts/dispatch_serial.mjs`, their generated rendering of the sprint-execution playbook, and its `dispatch-serial.md`. §22 applies unchanged. Differences from §23.1–§23.4:

- **Verdict (§23.1).** Same envelope, validated by `validateVerdicts(verdicts, { mode: 'serial' })`. `tokens` is either the measured object or exactly `{ "metering": "unavailable" }`; a non-GREEN verdict may carry `devSha: null` / `qaSha: null` when no commit exists. GREEN still requires both SHAs. The default mode is unchanged.
- **Attribution (§23.2).** There is no RUN_ID-keyed barrier row. The host's own dispatch hook chain attributes each role dispatch; when the host exposes no verifiable usage, nothing is written to the usage ledger — never a zero row.
- **Flashcards (§23.3).** The gate runs between every pair of consecutive stories (`cleargate-enforcement.md` §4.3) and is never suppressed.
- **Merge (§23.3).** DevOps merges each GREEN story as soon as it passes — one worktree at a time.
- **Blockers (§23.4).** A non-GREEN verdict halts the loop synchronously in the orchestrator's own turn; `dispatch_serial.mjs next --resume` re-dispatches only the blocked story after the human resolves it.
```

### enforcement §17 (canonical `scaffold/core/.cleargate/knowledge/cleargate-enforcement.md`, appended)

```
## 17. Host Dispatch Modes (source: STORY-058-12)

Each host adapter declares `dispatchMode` (`cleargate-cli/src/hosts/types.ts`): Claude Code `wave-parallel`, Codex `serial`. It is static and read at install time: `.agents/skills/sprint-execution/` — the generated serial rendering of the playbook plus `dispatch-serial.md` — is installed only for a selected host that declares the `.agents` shared root and `dispatchMode: serial`.

Under `dispatchMode: serial`:

1. **Flashcard gate.** `dispatch_serial.mjs next` refuses the next story while any `flashcards_flagged` card lacks its `.processed-<hash>` marker (the §4.6 scan, ported to `.cleargate/scripts/lib/flashcard-gate.mjs` and pinned to the hook by a parity test). The host dispatch hook still enforces §4.6 at every role dispatch. `SKIP_FLASHCARD_GATE` is never set in a serial run.
2. **Verdicts.** `dispatch_serial.mjs record` validates with `validateVerdicts(…, { mode: 'serial' })` and exits 3 on a non-GREEN verdict; the orchestrator halts in that turn.
3. **Worktrees.** The same command the wave path builds (`worktreeAddCommand`), one story at a time.
4. **Usage.** No usage-ledger row for `metering: unavailable`; `dispatch_serial.mjs` never writes `token-ledger.jsonl`.
```

- **Porting rule (new).** Bash ERE `.` and `[[:space:]]` both match `\r`, but JS `.` does not. Port:
  - every `.` as `[\s\S]`;
  - `[[:space:]]` as `[ \t\n\v\f\r]`;
  - the JSON string as `"((?:[^"\\]|\\[\s\S])*)"`;
  - `^[a-zA-Z_]` as ASCII.

  Otherwise JS drops the `\r` from CRLF list cards (a different hash) and misses a CRLF JSON open (`\[(.*)$`). Parity fixtures F6 and F13 kill that mutant.
- **Per-line check order** is exactly the hook's: JSON mode → inline `[]` → JSON open → YAML key → md heading → in-block stop → list item.
- Other semantics: unescape `\"` and then `\\`; list strip in the order leading `"`, trailing `"`, leading `'`, trailing `'`; skip empty cards; a trailing `''` split segment is a no-op.

````markdown
# Serial Dispatch Contract

This contract is the dispatch path for a host whose adapter declares `dispatchMode: serial` — a host with no Workflow primitive. It replaces the playbook's wave launch and nothing else: §22 (autonomy and the five true-blocker kinds), the per-story steps §C.1–§C.9, every role boundary, and every rule in `cleargate-enforcement.md` apply unchanged. A host that declares `dispatchMode: wave-parallel` never uses this file.

## 1. When this contract applies

- The installed playbook for this host names this file in §2 and §C.0.
- `dispatchMode` is fixed when ClearGate is installed. It is never chosen per session, and it is never a fallback for a host that has a Workflow primitive but cannot reach it — that host halts (§C.0).

## 2. The serial loop

Run the waves in `.cleargate/sprint-runs/<sprint-id>/plans/waves.json` order and, inside a wave, its stories in `stories` order. Exactly one story is in flight at any time, and inside a story exactly one role dispatch is in flight at any time.

**Contract-first plans.** A `waves.json` with `schema_version: 2` adds contracts and per-story `base` and `upstream`. A serial host ignores `contracts[]` and `base`: it runs the derived `waves` exactly as above, and it never starts a story before every story in its `upstream` has merged, so each story is cut from `sprint/S-NN` with its upstream already merged into it — there is no contract branch to create and no separate integration step.

1. Ask for the next action:
   `node .cleargate/scripts/dispatch_serial.mjs next --sprint <sprint-id> --wave <wave-id>`
   It prints one JSON object. Act on its `action`:
   - `process-flashcards` (exit 4) — process every listed card exactly as §C.9 says (approve or reject, then write its `.processed-<hash>` marker), rewrite every listed `unparseable` report's `flashcards_flagged` block as a `- "card"` list, then ask again.
   - `dispatch` (exit 0) — continue with step 2 for the named `storyId`.
   - `halt` (exit 3) — a recorded verdict for this story is not GREEN. Stop and surface its blocker to the human in this turn.
   - `wave-complete` (exit 0) — go to the next wave.
2. Create the story's worktree with exactly the printed `worktreeCommand` — `git worktree add .worktrees/STORY-X -b story/STORY-X sprint/S-NN` — unless `worktreeExists` is `true`.
3. Run the story through §C.1–§C.7. Each role works only inside `.worktrees/STORY-X`, plus its report under `.cleargate/sprint-runs/<sprint-id>/reports/`. Dispatch one role, wait for its final report, then decide the next dispatch. Never start a second role while one is still running.
4. Write the story's verdict (§5) to a file and record it:
   `node .cleargate/scripts/dispatch_serial.mjs record --sprint <sprint-id> --wave <wave-id> --verdict <file>`
   Exit 0: the verdict is GREEN — go back to step 1. Exit 3: the verdict is not GREEN — halt now, in this turn, and dispatch nothing else. Exit 1: the verdict is malformed — fix the verdict, never the validator.

## 3. Invariants reproduced

| Invariant | How the serial path keeps it |
|---|---|
| One ClearGate-managed worktree per story, cut from the sprint branch | `next` prints the command the wave path builds (`worktreeAddCommand` in `launch_wave.mjs`); worktrees are created one at a time |
| Flashcard write-gate per story (`cleargate-enforcement.md` §4.3) | `next` refuses to name the next story until every flagged card has a `.processed-<hash>` marker and no report's `flashcards_flagged` block is unparseable; the host's dispatch hook enforces the same gate (§4.6) at every role dispatch |
| Exactly-once dispatch attribution | the host's own dispatch hook chain attributes each role dispatch once (a dispatch marker or sentinel, claimed when the subagent stops); never write attribution by hand |
| Single-writer serial merge | DevOps merges each GREEN story to `sprint/S-NN` (§C.7) before the next story starts |
| True-blocker halt (§22) | a non-GREEN verdict halts the loop synchronously in the orchestrator's own turn |
| Idempotent resume | `next --resume` re-dispatches only the blocked story, reuses its worktree, and never re-dispatches a GREEN story |

## 4. Deliberately omitted

These three mechanisms exist only to work around a parallel wave; copying them would weaken the serial path.

| Mechanism (wave path) | Why the wave path has it | Why this contract omits it |
|---|---|---|
| `SKIP_FLASHCARD_GATE=1` for the whole wave | a parallel dispatch cannot give each segment its own environment, so the write-gate is relocated to the barrier | one story runs at a time, so the original per-story gate (§4.3) applies unmodified; setting the variable would silently widen the flashcard blind spot. Never set it during a serial run. |
| `RUN_ID`-keyed barrier ledger rows | under a Workflow run the dispatch hook never fires and the subagent stop event carries the orchestrator's session | serial dispatches go through the host's own dispatch hook chain; where the host exposes no verifiable usage, no usage row is written at all |
| Verdict returned instead of halting | a parallel run cannot stop for a human mid-run | the serial loop halts in its own turn, which is strictly stronger |

## 5. Verdict

Every story ends with one verdict object — the protocol §23.1 envelope, validated with `validateVerdicts(verdicts, { mode: 'serial' })`:

- `verdict` (`GREEN`, `ESCALATED` or `BLOCKED`), `storyId`, `runId` (the `runId` that `next` printed), `counters` (`qa_bounces`, `arch_bounces`, `breaker_hits`) and `flashcards_flagged` (the union of the dev and QA reports' cards).
- `devSha`, `qaSha`: required on GREEN; `null` on a non-GREEN verdict when that commit does not exist. Never invent a SHA.
- `tokens`: the measured object when the host reports verifiable usage, otherwise exactly `{ "metering": "unavailable" }`. Never zeros.
- `blocker` (`type`, `message`): required on a non-GREEN verdict; `type` is one of the five §22 kinds.

## 6. Resume after a blocker

After the human resolves a blocker, run `node .cleargate/scripts/dispatch_serial.mjs next --sprint <sprint-id> --wave <wave-id> --resume`. It names the blocked story again (`worktreeExists: true`). Run it from the step the blocker interrupted, record its new verdict, and continue with step 1. GREEN stories are never re-dispatched.
````

### F3. Role and agent listings (M5-A55)

- **No -13 check parses a Codex role listing.** `codex.live.roles` is not in `ENFORCEMENT_IDS` (M6:737, M5-A55 "-12 and -13 coupling"). `codex.roles` (verify-install) parses TOML files, never a listing.
- `codex.loop.dispatches` takes `agent_type` from three raw sources:
  - `JSON.parse(function_call.arguments).agent_type` for spawns;
  - the ` codex-identity ` log line via the token regex `(?:^| )agent_type=(\S+)(?: |$)`;
  - rollout `session_meta` via `JSON.parse` of each rollout line.
  Never a regex over `JSON.stringify` of any object.
- **Mock route markers match over the raw request body text** (`bodyText`, `mock-responses.mjs:47`), never over a re-serialized object. Every marker contains no `"`, `\` or control character, so its JSON encoding equals itself and a substring match is exact.
- **No marker may be a substring of another.** Test 20a asserts this. It is why S3/S4 use `CG-CONTROL-SPAWN-DENY` / `CG-CONTROL-SPAWN-ALLOW`, not M6's shared `CG-CONTROL-DISPATCH`.
- **Any -13 fixture that models the `spawn_agent` `agent_type` schema** (none is planned) uses the measured one-per-line layout: a header, `Available roles:`, then per role `<name>: {`, the description, `}`. Never a comma list.

- **Raw input.** Top-level keys:

- **Control ids.** The seven `codex.live.*` ids come from `codexHookVerdicts(inputs.controls)`, unchanged. Two overlays apply on top:
  1. **Human posture.** `codex.live.discovery` := `humanTrustDiscovery(registrations, trust.listing)` (a new pure export). It PASSes iff every registration has at least one listing entry with the same eventName/matcher/command, and every such entry is `source:'project'`, `enabled:true`, `trustStatus:'trusted'`. FAIL details are `missing: <Event> <command>` / `untrusted: <Event> <command>`. Reason: the owner trusts the hooks before `run`, so no untrusted listing is observable (flashcard 107).
  2. **Negative controls.** `codex.live.edit-deny` := `INCONCLUSIVE` iff the graded S1 attempt has zero `preToolUse` runs and `c3.probeExists === false`; detail `no gated tool call in <n> attempt(s); src/cg-probe.ts absent`. `codex.live.dispatch-deny` := `INCONCLUSIVE` iff the graded S3 attempt has zero `preToolUse` runs and no `subAgentActivity` item; detail `no gated tool call in <n> attempt(s); no subagent started`. In every other case the reused verdict stands; for example, zero runs with the file present stays FAIL.
- **Join rules.**
  - **`codex.loop.hook-matrix`**: a hook run belongs to an item when `run.id` ends with `:<item.id>` (X5, and -10's `codexPostToolUseVerdict` rule) and it is in the same `threadId`.
    - A `fileChange` item with `status:'completed'` needs a completed `preToolUse` and a completed `postToolUse`.
    - A blocked item needs a `blocked` `preToolUse` and no `postToolUse`.
    - A spawn needs a dispatch-gate `preToolUse`.
    - A dispatch needs a completed `subagentStop`.
    - A root session needs `sessionStart` completed exactly once.
  - **Measure first, in pass B's first scripted run:** whether code-mode-nested `apply_patch` produces `fileChange` items whose `id` equals the hook `run.id` suffix. If it does not, the Developer stops with a spec-gap blockers report quoting the measured ids (Architect amends); no join is invented.
  - **`commands`**: taken from `item/completed` items of type `commandExecution`, keyed by `params.threadId` (`commandSource: 'items'`). If pass B's first scripted run shows that nested `exec_command` calls produce no `commandExecution` item, they are taken from the per-thread rollouts (`commandSource: 'rollouts'`). The evidence prints the source, and the dev report records the measured shape.
- **`codex.loop.dispatches`** joins each dispatch to exactly one identity line by `agent_id` = child `threadId`, and checks the line's `agent_type` against the rollout `session_meta.agent_role`. Work item is recorded, not required.
- **`codex.loop.serial-verdict`** additionally requires `recordExitCode === 0` (F6.8). It reads the last `STORY-001-01` line of `SPRINT-01/serial/wave1.verdicts.jsonl`; the extra `recorded_at` key is ignored by `validateVerdicts`.
- **Result.** `result` = PASS iff all of these hold:
  - `loop_transport` PASS and `enforcement_parity` PASS;
  - `verifyInstallExit === 0` and `doctorExit === 0`;
  - for `posture: 'human'`: `configWrites === 0`, and `configBefore`/`configAfter` deep-equal on `hooks.state` and `projects["<roomReal>"]`.

### TPV13-A2. Hook joins and dispatch facts (measured; replaces the F6.6 join bullets and M6:792/799 where they differ)

- Every hook run is attributed by `params.threadId`, the thread it ran on. A tool hook's `run.id` ends with `:<call id>`. A code-mode `apply_patch` produces a `fileChange` item whose `id` is that call id (`exec-<uuid>`) on the same thread (P2), so F6.6's "measure first" stop does **not** trigger: the join holds.
- A nested `exec_command` produces an `item/completed` `commandExecution` item on the calling thread with `command = "/bin/zsh -c '<cmd>'"` and `exitCode`, `source: 'unifiedExecStartup'`. `commandSource` is `'items'`; the rollout fallback is never needed. Verdicts match commands by **containment**, never equality.
- A spawn is a root-thread `subAgentActivity` item with `kind:'started'`, `id` = the spawn call id, `agentThreadId` = the child. Its dispatch gate is the root-thread `preToolUse` run whose id ends `:<that id>`. `item/started` and `item/completed` both carry `kind:'started'`; dedupe by item id.
- **SubagentStop runs on the child thread** (`params.threadId === agentThreadId`) with a suffix-less id (`subagent-stop:<n>:<hooks.json>`). Join a dispatch to its SubagentStop by thread, never by run id.
- **No SubagentStart.** The Codex install registers five hooks (SessionStart, PreToolUse ×2, PostToolUse, SubagentStop). M6:792's "exactly one SubagentStart" is deleted: `codex.loop.dispatches` requires exactly one completed SubagentStop on the child thread.
- **Serial interval** = [the first `subAgentActivity` `kind:'started'` for T, the first `kind:'completed'|'interrupted'` for T], by notification order; intervals must not overlap. This replaces "child `turn/started`→idle". The terminal item (`id: subagent-completed-<child turn>`) is a separate root-thread item that arrives after the child's SubagentStop.
- SessionStart: exactly once on the root thread of each root session, never on a child.
- **`codex.loop.hook-matrix` grades S5 only** (`loop.notifications`, root = `loop.rootThreadId`): exactly one completed root SessionStart and none elsewhere; every completed `fileChange` has a completed preToolUse and a completed postToolUse (suffix + same thread); a `blocked` preToolUse has no postToolUse with its suffix; every spawn has its dispatch gate; every dispatch has a completed SubagentStop on its thread. S1–S4 hooks stay graded by the reused `codexHookVerdicts`; the rendered matrix shows their rows informationally.
- `codex.loop.dispatches`: dispatch agent_type = its one identity line (joined by `agent_id` = child thread); cross-check = the child rollout's `session_meta.payload.agent_role` (`JSON.parse` per line). F3's spawn-arguments source is recorded when the root rollout is present, never required.
- `<room>` for `codex.loop.worktree` = `loop.gitWorktreeList[0].path` (the main worktree).

### TPV13-A3. `codexLoopVerdicts` raw-input contract (QA-Red's rendering, pinned)

`loop.notifications` = raw S5 notifications (all threads) · `loop.identityLines` = raw ` codex-identity ` lines appended during S5 · `loop.rollouts` = `{[childAgentId]: raw rollout text}` · `loop.commands` = `[{threadId, command, exitCode}]` from `commandExecution` items · `loop.gitWorktreeList` = `[{path, branch}]` from `git worktree list --porcelain` · `loop.gitBranches` = short names · `loop.mergeCommit` = `{sha, parents}` · `loop.storyHeadSha` · `loop.lsTree` = paths at `sprint/S-01` · `loop.stateJson` = parsed state.json **`.stories`** map · `loop.eventsJsonl` = raw lines · `loop.serialLog` = parsed JSON objects, one per line · `loop.recordExitCode` = the exit code of the command containing `dispatch_serial.mjs record` · `loop.importProbe` string · `loop.npmTestExit` number · `loop.served` = mock `served` (scripted) or `[]` · `pathIdentity` = `{hookSide, roleShell, expected}` · `roomLedgers` = `{[rel]: text}` (every value empty) · `metaRepoAppended` = `{[rel]: appendedText}` · `trust.configBefore/After` = `{'hooks.state': subtree, 'projects["<roomReal>"]': subtree}`, compared whole · `attempts` = `{S1, S2a, S2b, S3, S4}`.
- The returned record holds the 17 gating ids, the INFO rows `codex.loop.metering` (detail starts `unavailable`; per-dispatch `childUsage` rows), `codex.loop.trust-posture`, `codex.loop.wall-clock`, and the strings `loop_transport`, `enforcement_parity`, `result`.
- `serial-verdict` requires `tokens` deep-equal `{metering:'unavailable'}` **in addition to** `validateVerdicts` (a complete measured object passes `validateVerdicts`).
- `childUsage`: `records` = the `token_usage_record` count; `matchesProvider` is `null` without `served`, else true iff every record joins a served entry by `response_id` and `input_tokens`, `cached_input_tokens`←`input_tokens_details.cached_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `reasoning_output_tokens`←`output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` and `total_tokens` all equal (P3 measured).

## Post-flight rulings (STORY-058-13, 2026-09-27; role: architect; append-only)

Source: `reports/STORY-058-13-arch.md` (VERDICT: FAIL, one blocking finding, plan-origin). Binding for STORY-058-13; wins over M6:794, F6.6 and TPV13-A2/A3 where they differ. No Gherkin, scope, file-list or test-count change.

**PF13-A1: Root-thread `update_state` rule (replaces M6:794's `update_state.mjs` entry; B1).**

### BUG-100 — Codex sandbox writable root (cli)

| Aspect | Blueprint |
|---|---|
| Files / functions | `src/init/inject-codex-config.ts`:<br>• `planCodexConfig(existing, pinVersion, file, opts?: { writableRoot?: string \| null })`, additive; the first three params are unchanged (C1 frozen shape).<br>• `PlanCodexConfigResult` gains `writableRoot: 'added' \| 'replaced' \| 'unchanged' \| 'none'`.<br>• `injectCodexConfig(cwd, pinVersion, opts?: { resolveGitCommonDir?: (cwd) => string \| null })`: the default runs `git -C <cwd> rev-parse --git-common-dir`, then `path.resolve(cwd, out)`, then `fs.realpathSync`; not a git repo gives `null`.<br>• New export `removeCodexWritableRoot(existing, root, file) → { next, removed }`.<br>• `assertCodexConfigParsable` also runs the sandbox scan (placeholder root `/__cleargate_preflight__/.git`), so preflight refuses before any write, exactly as for the existing keys.<br><br>`src/hosts/codex.ts`:<br>• `install()` (`:115-129`) passes nothing new; `injectCodexConfig` resolves the root.<br>• A 5th `Codex:` line prints when the root is written (pinned below).<br>• `remove()` (`:209-223`) also calls `removeCodexWritableRoot(raw, realpath(common dir) ?? realpath(cwd)/.git, file)`.<br>• `CodexAdapterDeps` gains `removeCodexWritableRoot` (the DEFAULT_DEPS pattern). |
| Pinned rules | 1. Owned root = realpath of the git common dir. That is the main `.git`, and it covers `.worktrees/*`, whose index and refs live there.<br>2. ### A2. Build set, lanes and bundling

- **Contracts: none.**
  - Every lane's `base` is cli `main` at lane open.
  - Outer `story/<lead>` is cut from `sprint/S-41` for two-repo lanes; cli-only lanes use `--detach sprint/S-41`.
  - Integration follows rule 21.
- **Decision (OD-M7-12): four lanes, not ten.**
  1. **The merge lane is the binding constraint.** Each merge costs an integration, the full suite (~7 min at ~3.7k tests), BD and a boundary step; two of the four lanes (M7-A, M7-B) also need an RS.
     - Ten lanes would mean ten such cycles and about 50 dispatches. Four lanes mean four cycles and about 22 dispatches.
     - All 4 build lanes are busy now (101/100/047/103), with 102/105/104/106 queued.
     - With bundles, the whole addendum fits in the second round of lane openings.
  2. **Bundles follow file ownership, so no two lanes edit the same region.**
     - M7-A owns every edit to `qa.md`'s RED section and to SKILL §C.3, §C.3.5, §C.5, §C.7 and §D.5.1.
     - M7-B owns the main-checkout resolution concept (written once in bash for 107a, once in mjs for 110) and every twin script except `close_sprint.mjs`.
     - The only file shared across lanes is `run_script.sh`: M7-A edits `:133-242`, M7-B edits `:63-79`. The hunks are disjoint.
  3. **BUG-114 stands alone.** It is P1, and must not wait behind text bugs.
  4. **BUG-112 stands alone.** Its re-scope of merged sealed -11 tests is a separate TPV surface.
  5. **M7-B lists the M7-A members as upstream.** M7-A then creates the new init-fixture rows the two lanes share (`run_script.sh`, `developer.md`), and M7-B appends to them. The order is deterministic, so QA-Red re-seals once.

| Lane | Lead (worktree name) | Members, in lane order | Repo | Upstream (union) | Opens (lane_priority) | TPV | Boundary after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M7-C | BUG-114 | 114 | both (twin `close_sprint.mjs`; twin `bug076_077_close_path.red.sh`) | — | after BUG-105 opens | live | BD |
| M7-A | BUG-108 | 108 → 109 → 113 → 115 → 116 | both (BUG-109's `run_script.sh` twin) | BUG-103 | after M7-C | scan-gated | BD, RS-M7d |
| M7-B | BUG-110 | 110 → 111 → 107 | both | BUG-102, BUG-103, BUG-105, all M7-A members | after M7-A | live | BD, RS-M7e |
| M7-D | BUG-112 | 112 | cli (outer detached) | BUG-101 | after BUG-106 | live | BD |

**Bundle protocol (binding for M7-A and M7-B).**
1. **Worktrees.** One outer worktree and one nested cli worktree per lane, named after the lead: `.worktrees/<lead>`, with branch `story/<lead>` in each repo (rule 19).
2. **Dispatch.** One dispatch per role per lane.
   - Line 1 of every brief is `<lead> (M7-<X> bundle: <member ids in lane order>)`.
   - The brief cites each member's §A4 section.
   - The token ledger attributes the lane's cost to the lead. The Reporter discloses this.
3. **Commits.** One commit per bug per role, in lane order: `qa-red(BUG-NNN): …`, then `fix(EPIC-058): BUG-NNN …`.
   - No commit spans two bugs.
   - CHANGELOG gets one `### Fixed` line per bug, inside that bug's commit.
4. **Verdicts are per bug.**
   - QA-Verify writes one PASS/FAIL row per member.
   - A FAIL re-dispatches the Developer for that member only, and increments only that member's `qa_bounces`.
   - An `Escalated` member leaves the bundle through a `git revert` of its commits on the lane branch (no history rewrite) and is re-planned. The rest of the bundle still merges.
5. **State.**
   - `validate_bounce_readiness` and every `update_state` transition run per member id.
   - DevOps does one merge (outer, then cli), one full suite, one BD and one boundary step, then `update_state <id> Done` for each member.
6. **Reports.** `<lead>-{qa-red,dev,qa,arch,devops}.md`, each with a `## Per-bug` section and one `flashcards_flagged` block.
7. **Surface gate.** BUG ids resolve to no file, so the gate skips (flashcard 215). No bypass is needed on the lane branch.

### A4. Per-bug blueprint

**Common to every addendum item.** These rules add to M7 §3's "Common to all items".
- **Leaf counting.**
  - Each `Tn` is one `test()`. Iterate over targets inside the test body.
  - Counts are `ℹ tests` leaf counts (E30).
- **Spawned children.**
  - Remove `ORCHESTRATOR_PROJECT_DIR`, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, `CLEARGATE_STATE_FILE`, `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_WORK_TREE` from the child's env.
  - Set `PATH` explicitly: `/usr/bin:/bin` plus exactly what the test needs. The global 0.26.1 `cleargate` sits beside `node` and `jq` in `/opt/homebrew/bin`, so put any stub directory **first**.
  - Compare paths through `fs.realpathSync`, because macOS maps `/var` to `/private/var`.
- **Scripts under test.** Either copy them with their siblings, `lib/` included, into a temp git repo (flashcard 1), or spawn them in place from `scaffold/core` via `canonicalPath()`.
- **New SKILL.md and role text** carries none of the following:
  - a `CODEX_SKILL_BANNED` token (`build-codex-payload.mjs:264-276`);
  - an anchor-prefix line (`:297-307`);
  - `Skill(` (M7-D's guard throws on it).
- **Text tests** read the canonical file and the tracked generated copy: `scaffold/core/.agents/skills/sprint-execution/SKILL.md` and `scaffold/hosts/codex/.codex/agents/<role>.toml`.
- **Rule 16** applies to M7-A and M7-B: run the `CLEARGATE_META_ROOT` file list in the nested worktree, with no override.
- **Escapes in pinned texts.** Inside a code span, `\`` stands for a literal backtick and, in table cells, `\|` stands for a literal `|` — the M7 §3 convention. Write the unescaped characters into the file.

### A10. Risks, open decisions, follow-ups

#### Risks

| # | Risk | Control |
|---|---|---|
| R-10 | One failing member blocks a bundle's merge. | Verdicts are per bug. An Escalated member leaves the bundle through `git revert` (§A2 protocol 4). |
| R-11 | In a consumer repo, BUG-114's PATH candidate can select a skewed global dist, whose older reconcile code then runs close. | close prints the dist it uses; BUG-104's resolver line exposes the skew; DT uses the cli main symlink (P11). |
| R-12 | After RS-M7e, the live meta-repo hook skips delivery edits in outer worktrees. | Rule 20: amendments are made in the main checkout. Stories tick Task Breakdown rows in commits, which is unaffected. |
| R-13 | A close_sprint test that spawns with the ambient PATH breaks on a machine with a global `cleargate`. | E25 re-scopes; the M7-C merge-lane witness runs every spawner with the ambient PATH. |
| R-14 | `/reports/` reaches only fresh or re-initialised installs, and only once `.cleargate/.gitignore` is committed. | DT commits the install. FU-11 covers `upgrade`. |
| R-15 | `LAYER_COUNTS` is self-reported. | TPV re-counts on the flagged path; QA-Verify still traces coverage; FU-14. |
| R-16 | M7-B waits on six earlier merges and becomes the tail. | It builds from base `main` in parallel and integrates once. Its hook and lock work is re-applied at integration (owner wins, rule 21). |

## Amendments from TPV (BUG-100, 2026-09-27; role: architect; append-only)

- **TPV100-A1 (preflight root; replaces the §3 BUG-100 bullet "`assertCodexConfigParsable` also runs the sandbox scan (placeholder root `/__cleargate_preflight__/.git`)").** `assertCodexConfigParsable(cwd)` resolves the root exactly as `injectCodexConfig` does (same default resolver, same optional `{ resolveGitCommonDir }` seam) and calls `planCodexConfig(existing, '0.0.0', file, { writableRoot: root })`. A null root (non-git cwd) skips the sandbox scan. Reason: with the placeholder, preflight refuses an inline/dotted definition that already holds the real root, so rule 3's exception is unreachable through `init`/`host add`, and it refuses a non-git install that the write leaves byte-identical (rule 4, E12). Pinned by re-sealed Test 8b.
- **TPV100-A2 (stale rule and outcome labels; §3 BUG-100 rule 2, OD-M7-7).** An element is a stale ClearGate root iff it is an absolute path, its last segment is `.git`, it is not equal to `<root>`, and `fs.existsSync(element)` is false. Relative elements are never stale (Codex ignores them; their existence depends on the process cwd). The first stale element becomes `<root>` when `<root>` is absent; further stale elements are dropped. `writableRoot` is `'replaced'` when any stale element was replaced or dropped, `'added'` when `<root>` was appended (new table, inserted key or appended element), `'unchanged'` when `<root>` was already present with nothing stale (or an inline/dotted definition already holds it), and `'none'` when no root was given.
- **TPV100-A3 (notice condition; §3 BUG-100 "Notice (pinned)").** The fifth `Codex:` line prints after the four existing `Codex:` lines on every install whose resolved root is non-null (`writableRoot` `added`, `replaced` or `unchanged`); never in a non-git cwd. Pinned by re-sealed Tests 1 and 2.
- **TPV100-A4 (counts; §2.3 row 2 and §3 BUG-100 D4).** BUG-100's red file has 10 tests (8 red, 2 anchors), not 7: default-tier Δ +10. Every §2.3 row from #2 on shifts by +3 (row 2 = 3669 / 3667); the final projection is 3702 / 3700 / 0 fail / 2 skip if the other items' counts hold.
- **TPV100-A5 (resolver env; §3 BUG-100 Gotchas).** The default resolver deletes `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE` and `GIT_COMMON_DIR` from its child env. Measured: a pre-commit hook in a linked worktree receives `GIT_DIR=<main>/.git/worktrees/<wt>`, which would otherwise turn any cwd, git or not, into that repo's common dir. Pinned (GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE) by re-sealed Test 2.

- **Orchestrator reconciliation (2026-09-27T09:48Z):** TPV100-A4 (+10 after the re-seal) supersedes the addendum A5 figure for BUG-100 (+8). Every A5 running total from the BUG-100 row on shifts by +2; the provisional end is **3748 / 3746 / 0 fail / 2 skip**. BUG-103 is still +20 provisionally, pending its TPV. `arch_bounces` BUG-100 = 1.

## Amendments from TPV (BUG-047, 2026-09-27; role: architect; append-only)

- **TPV047-A1 — the `>=` boundary is load-bearing.** `last_gate_check == updated_at` is fresh at all four sites: the `writeCachedGate` early return, the Check 5 item site (`:1665`), the plan site (`:1709`) and `restoreIfOnlyTimestampMoved`. The stamp-and-gate hook writes both fields in the same second, so a `>` build rewrites every hook-gated item and re-dirties main on the first post-BD preflight. The re-seal pins the boundary in T2 (item and plan), T3(b) and T5 C.
- **TPV047-A2 — freshness is pass-independent.** A stale item with an unchanged **failing** verdict advances (`writeCachedGate`) and keeps its Step-0 stamp (restore guard). A fresh failing item stays byte-identical on a rerun, which is CR-038's original kickoff case. Re-seal: T1's failing half, T3(c), T5 D.
- **TPV047-A3 — stale verdict change and plan-site staleness.** A stale item whose verdict changes gets the new verdict written, not only a new stamp (T4, second half). The plan site's staleness had no test anywhere. T2 phase 2 pins the E13 remedy: stamp the plan → Check 5 `- SPRINT-01 (stale)` → `gate check <plan>` → exit 0. Step 0 still does not refresh the plan (OD-M7-11 / FU-5 unchanged).
- **TPV047-A4 — re-scope watch, sole killers.**
  - `test/lib/frontmatter-writers.red.node.test.ts:413` has no `updated_at`, so it is fresh via `updatedAt === ''`. It is the sole killer of an "empty `updated_at` is stale" build.
  - sprint-preflight Scenarios 11 and 16 are the sole killers of "item site never stale".
  - Scenario 20 "a genuine verdict change is NOT reverted" is the sole killer of "restore ignores the verdict comparison".
  - All three stay unmodified. BUG-047's count is unchanged: +5 (3671 / 3669).
- **TPV047-A5 — R-5 refinement.** After BUG-047's BD, only strictly stale live items (`last_gate_check < updated_at`) rewrite on their next gate; items at the boundary do not. Check 5 now reports a hand-written `pass: true` cache without a `last_gate_check` as `stale`; `gate check` clears it.

- **Orchestrator note (2026-09-27T10:17Z):** BUG-047 re-seal keeps the count at 5 (D4 +5 unchanged). `arch_bounces` BUG-047 = 1. Incident during this TPV: a shared-scratchpad collision reset two BUG-100 worktree files (the BUG-100 Developer was notified to re-verify).
